title: Moonquakes
purpose: Teach that Apollo seismometers recorded shallow moonquakes, how strong they were, and why equipment on the Moon is latched down.

beats.label: measured
beats.credit: NASA PDS · Apollo Passive Seismic Experiment (Nakamura et al.)

beats.credit: What a quake does to a room

beats.label: measured
beats.card: Recorded by stations near the equator
beats.sub: The polar quake's position is uncertain; the story's quake is fiction

captions: Apollo astronauts left seismometers on the Moon, and the ground moved.
From {first} to {last} they recorded {count} shallow moonquakes.
The strongest reached magnitude {max}: enough to rattle a base.
A quake shakes anything that is not held down.
That is why equipment on the Moon is strapped and latched.
These were recorded far from the south pole.
ends_on: Before the ground shakes, latch what matters. Loose things fall.
